gen-gf-phudu-gf-fenix: Fenix writes in a classic, editorial serif whose curves stop before turning inward. Phudu, bold and drawn like a ballpoint line, sits beside it feeling brash next to Fenix's bookish manners.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-gentium-plus: Phudu is bold, drawn with a ballpoint's plain, pressure-free weight. Gentium Plus is a refined serif with a pitcher's wide mouth in each c, and that classic poise against the flat bold heading is the draw.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-gowun-batang: Gowun Batang is a refined, literary serif with terminals cut back. Beside Phudu's loud, ballpoint-plain strokes it reads like a quiet voice after a shout, and the two share the page without crowding.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-habibi: Strokes as plain as a ballpoint line give Phudu its bold, distinctive look. And Habibi, a traditional classic serif with a clear channel into each round letter, supplies the editorial counterweight.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-inika: Distinctive in its ballpoint-plain line, Phudu leaves generous openings on every curve. But Inika, a classic serif with a see-through gap in each s, brings a traditional, settled voice that lets the heading be loud.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-kay-pho-du: Generous openings on every curve, drawn in a plain ballpoint line, mark Phudu as bold. Kay Pho Du is a traditional serif whose counters breathe like a hollow reed, so paragraphs of it should move along smoothly.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-labrada: Labrada reads dignified and bookish, a classic serif with wide openings on its small letters. And Phudu, constant in stroke width and bold, earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-laila: Bold, with a ballpoint's plain line, Phudu leaves generous openings on every curve. Laila, a traditional serif with space between curve ends and stem, takes the supporting part so the heading can lead.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-montaga: Bold curves with generous openings, all in one pressure-free line, make Phudu hard to miss. Montaga, a classic serif with pen-lifted curves left unfinished, should read like stitched thread across a paragraph.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-new-tegomin: New Tegomin reads dignified and traditional, a classic serif whose c looks like a wide-open ring. Whole paragraphs of it settle in easily, well away from Phudu's blunt display.
